fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Reading the chart through the body", "body": "Emily Ridout describes AstroYoga as astrology that literally affects the body, with the body then used to navigate the sky map toward where a person wants to go. She says that can mean yoga postures, mudra and mantra, or simply choosing activities that resonate the way a placement needs. A first birth chart reading has value, she says, but clients who return month after month get far deeper and more specific advice. She closes by describing her Astrology Academy course starting in January, her on demand AstroYoga teacher training, and memberships with group sessions and a monthly booklet of roughly fifty pages."}, {"title": "Relative truth and holding others in loving awareness", "body": "With Mars entering Sagittarius and crossing the lunar south node, Emily says the hallmark of the Sagittarius and Gemini nodes is mistaking a relative truth for the ultimate truth. She argues this is a moment to trust lived experience, the body and intuition over authority, while admitting that opinions, like a favorite ice cream flavor, are meant to stay relative. Heading into the holidays, Chance says meeting family where they are works better than arguing, since our energy is the one thing we control. Emily adds that a frustrating argument reflects something about ourselves, and that no problem is solved at the level at which it was created."}, {"title": "Freedom versus structure in 2021", "body": "Emily names the Saturn in Aquarius and Uranus in Taurus square as the hallmark of 2021, likening it to the myth of Ouranos and Kronos at war. In her reading, Saturn brings restriction, from online censorship to the useful structure of organizing a podcast, while Uranus brings freedom, chaos and surprise, so people wrestled with questions like staying single or marrying. Chance recalls a day that left him with new respect for Saturn's boundaries. Emily also says native Plutonians born roughly from 1984 into the early 1990s met a Uranus opposition that resurfaced old shadow, and that Chiron in Aries exposes where we traded our true self for safety."}, {"title": "Venus retrograde and love that starts within", "body": "Emily describes Venus joining Pluto in Capricorn, which she links to the Persephone and Hades story as an allegory for winter, before Venus stations retrograde. In her view beauty is then best sought within, so it is a poor moment to shop for clothes or hunt for a new partner and Capricorn's rule over antiquity invites looking back through folklore and tarot. Chance offers his own view that the only kind of love is self-love, with care for others as its verb, so nobody runs a love deficit. Emily adds the tarot image of cups brought full to the party, and asks couples to separate love from attachment."}, {"title": "What 2022 may bring, in Emily's reading", "body": "Emily calls Jupiter entering Pisces to join Neptune the hallmark of 2022, with an exact conjunction around April that she believes could help many people move from knowing esoteric principles to consciously directing them. She ties Pisces to the Moon card, and asks listeners to keep up meditation and to rest, since she says those shifts happen during sleep. She raises floods and waves as a possible pitfall, and Chance mentions Cliff High's web bot forecasting glacial movement. Emily also flags the lunar nodes moving into Taurus and Scorpio in January, the eclipse axis of seed and flower, and a United States Pluto return."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Emily Ridout is an astrologer, folklorist and master yogini, who's been a frequent returning guest for InnerVerse. Combining her multiple disciplines, Emily not only reads your sky-clock chart, she combines that wisdom with your unique physiology by prescribing movement practices that are perfect for your planetary placements. Today we're going live with this Astro-Yoga guru to talk about 2021 and 2022.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chance's natal chart as a live teaching case", "body": "In the members' hour, Emily Ridout reads Chance Garton's natal chart on air as a worked example for listeners. She starts from his Leo ascendant at ten degrees, which she says points to knowing himself through his own sovereign spirit, then turns to his north node in Pisces and south node in Virgo. Emily reads that axis as a call to release control over money and values and move into collective depth and healing. She ties his eighth house stellium to shadow work, and Chance adds that for him shadow work lives in the body and in tending his own physical health."}, {"title": "Grand trines, a Libra moon and one on one talk", "body": "Emily Ridout points to what she calls a grand trine linking Chance Garton's moon, Mars and Jupiter with his descendant, the point she says rules one on one relationships. She jokes that interviewing guests one at a time temporarily completes that trine. Emily describes his full Libra moon in the third house as a pattern of high highs and low lows, and suggests noticing which settings bring each. Chance describes his habit of hopping from mountaintop to mountaintop, while Emily counters that the low points are also teachers and that becoming the fulcrum of the scale beats chasing only the highs."}, {"title": "Freedom, daily joy and leaving the day job", "body": "Emily Ridout reads Chance Garton's Capricorn stellium, starting with Vesta, as a need to create something joyful every day in a businesslike way, and Uranus as a tiny inner anarchist that resists routine. Chance connects this to the custom graphics he makes for every show and the crystal layouts he builds for remote sound healing sessions. He describes cutting his day job to around ten hours a week, taking on clients and guest spots, and argues that setting firm boundaries around what he enjoys lets the world reorganize itself around him. Emily frames his cardinal T-square as an engine that stalls, then surges."}, {"title": "Chiron in Cancer and guarding creative time", "body": "Emily Ridout points out that in Chance Garton's chart Vesta sits opposite Chiron at one degree of Cancer, the start of what she calls the mother archetype, a placement she ties to nurture, home and the old wounds carried from early life. Chance describes how protective he has become of his time as he steps back from a day job to put more of himself into the show. Emily frames his central Chiron question as whether he gets to direct his own time and creative output, and suggests that healing here comes from claiming that freedom without guilt."}, {"title": "Surrender, synchronicity and the chart as a map", "body": "Emily Ridout says she has been contemplating Pluto and Pisces and what it means to surrender control and let grace move through a life. She shares stories from her years in India, her initiation in a meditation tradition centered on Shiva, and a stranger's wallet delivered to her door that led to a shared crystal seller. Chance Garton links synchronicity to pattern and to calling both future and past selves through time. Asked whether a chart can predict such moments, Emily says it shows potential and tendencies, not fixed outcomes, and Chance argues the best astrologers widen possibility rather than declare fate."}]
